topic_brief.title: No-till vs conventional tillage effects on crop yield
topic_brief.research_question: Does no-till management affect crop yield compared to conventional tillage, and how does this vary by crop type and climate?
topic_brief.population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing tillage systems
topic_brief.intervention_description: No-till or zero-till management (seeds planted directly into undisturbed soil)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional tillage (moldboard plow, disk, chisel, or other inversion/intensive tillage)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is NO-TILL (less disturbance), Control is CONVENTIONAL TILLAGE (more disturbance)
Reduced tillage is NOT no-till - if both exist, compare no-till vs conventional
Some papers have 3+ tillage levels - extract the no-till vs most intensive tillage comparison
Strip-till is intermediate - do not include as no-till unless paper explicitly calls it no-till
Long-term trials may show different effects in early vs late years - extract each year separately
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall -5.7%; Wheat -2.6%; Maize -7.6%; Rice -7.5%; Soybean +0.3%; Oilseed rape -9.0%

rows.title: Weed dynamics and productivity of wheat (Triticum aestivum) under various tillage and weed management practices
rows.treatment_description: Zero tillage (ZT), direct seeding with zero-till ferti-cum-seed drill, rice residues retained on surface
rows.control_description: Conventional tillage (CT), standard tillage practices
rows.notes: Treatment mean (40.08 q/ha) explicitly stated in text. Control mean (~34 q/ha) estimated from Figure 1 bar chart. SE values (~3 q/ha each) estimated from figure error bars with low precision. Paper has T1/T2 label inconsistency: methodology defines T1=ZT and T2=CT, but weed density/biomass data in Table 1 show T2 with lower weed counts, which the text attributes to zero tillage. However, the yield text unambiguously states 'Zero tillage produced a maximum yield of 40.08 q/ha' matching T1 as the taller bar in Figure 1. Number of replications not stated (likely 3 based on typical Indian agricultural experimental designs). LSD used for mean comparisons (P=0.05) but LSD value for yield not reported. The positive effect (+17.9%) for no-till contradicts the expected negative direction but is consistent with rice-wheat systems in the Indo-Gangetic Plains where ZT with residue retention often increases wheat yield. Single-season study (2021-22). Weed management was a subplot factor with 9 levels; yield data reported only as tillage main-effect means averaged across weed management practices.

moderators.mod_residue_management: retained (rice residues on surface under ZT)

rows.title: Effect of Conservation Agricultural and Nitrogen Management Practices on Productivity, Profitability, Nutrient-uptake and Response Functions of N-fertilization in Wheat
rows.outcome: grain yield at economic optimum N
rows.treatment_description: Zero tillage flat bed (ZT-F) at N_opt=133.1 kg N/ha
rows.control_description: Conventional tillage flat bed (CT-F) at N_opt=128.3 kg N/ha
rows.notes: Grain yield derived from quadratic response functions at each treatment's economic optimum N dose. CAUTION: treatment and control are at DIFFERENT N levels (133.1 vs 128.3 kg/ha), so comparison is confounded by N rate. No variance reported. Data from 2010-11 only.

rows.title: Effect of Conservation Agricultural and Nitrogen Management Practices on Productivity, Profitability, Nutrient-uptake and Response Functions of N-fertilization in Wheat
rows.outcome: grain yield at economic optimum N
rows.treatment_description: Zero tillage raised bed (ZT-B) at N_opt=132.9 kg N/ha
rows.control_description: Conventional tillage raised bed (CT-B) at N_opt=135.3 kg N/ha
rows.notes: Grain yield from quadratic response at economic optimum N. ZT-B yielded LESS than CT-B even at optimum N. Treatment and control at similar but not identical N levels. No variance. 2010-11 only.

rows.title: Effect of Conservation Agricultural and Nitrogen Management Practices on Productivity, Profitability, Nutrient-uptake and Response Functions of N-fertilization in Wheat
rows.outcome: grain yield at economic optimum N
rows.treatment_description: Zero tillage flat bed with residue (ZT-F+R) at N_opt=172.1 kg N/ha
rows.control_description: Conventional tillage flat bed (CT-F) at N_opt=128.3 kg N/ha
rows.notes: Grain yield from quadratic response at economic optimum N. CAUTION: N_opt for ZT-F+R (172.1) is 44 kg/ha higher than CT-F (128.3), meaning much of the yield advantage may be due to higher N, not tillage. Paper notes ZT+R requires ~50 kg additional N. No variance. 2010-11 only.
